entities.summary: Matteo Rosso Orsini, a Roman aristocrat and diplomat, played a pivotal role in shaping the course of European history during the 13th century. Born into a noble family, Orsini rose through the ranks of the Roman Catholic Church, becoming a cardinal under Pope Nicholas III in 1277. Orsini's diplomatic skills and strategic alliances helped to secure key territories and influence the decisions of European monarchs. One of his most notable achievements was the negotiation of the Treaty of Lucera, which secured the safety of the Papal States in 1278. Orsini's legacy extends beyond his diplomatic exploits, as he also contributed to the development of the Catholic Church's administrative structures and helped to promote the interests of the Roman aristocracy. Despite his significant influence, Orsini's life was marked by controversy, including allegations of corruption and bribery. His eventual death in 1305 marked the end of an era, as the balance of power in Europe continued to shift in the decades that followed. The Orsini family's legacy would go on to shape the course of Italian history for centuries to come, with Matteo's nephew, Pope Nicholas III, playing a significant role in the development of the Catholic Church during the 14th century.
